text.p: French aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney said Thursday that provisions for a cost-cutting plan would push the group in the red in 1996.
Chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier told a news conference that provisions for the two billion francs ($389 million) restructuring plan would result in a loss for the year.
First half net income fell to 426 million francs ($83 million) in the first half of 1996 from 658 million francs ($128 million) in the same period for 1995.
The company predicted earlier 1996 earnings would drop, citing the absence of signs of an economic recovery in Europe and volatile aluminium prices.

Pechiney's cost-cutting plan seeks to find four bilion francs ($778 million) in cost savings by the end of 1998. Along with these savings, investments of about 3.5 billion francs ($681 million) will be made over the next three years.
In the first half of 1996, Pechiney faced a worldwide reduction in demand from primary aluminium stemming from a sluggish European economy.
